record.title: RACER reports role-based competence estimates for routing to unseen human experts
record.summary: A September 18 work-in-progress preprint proposes RACER, which estimates an unseen expert’s query-level probability of being correct from a small context set using class-role relationships rather than absolute class identities. The authors prove a coherent class-relabelling invariance result, derive a Bayes-aligned deferral surrogate and provide a regret bound. In experiments, they report gains on synthetic expert benchmarks and budget-swept performance described as competitive or best on VinDr-CXR and CheXpert. On CheXpert, RACER-C and RACER-kernel report similar primary AURSBAC means (0.7243 and 0.7241 over 27 matched cells); the paper labels the comparisons descriptive and makes no significance claim. VinDr-CXR results use training annotations because official test labels lack radiologist identities; an out-of-distribution expert group is inferred from co-annotation patterns. Results remain author-reported and the code is not yet released.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: RACER estimates an unseen expert’s query-level probability of being correct from a small context set using role-relative class relations; the paper gives a coherent class-relabelling invariance result, a Bayes-aligned deferral surrogate and a plug-in regret bound.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that RACER variants are competitive or best in budget-swept deferral on VinDr-CXR and CheXpert. On CheXpert, RACER-C and RACER-kernel have primary seen-plus-unseen AURSBAC means of 0.7243 and 0.7241 over 27 matched cells; the preprint calls comparisons descriptive and makes no significance claim.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish clinical utility or transfer to deployment: VinDr-CXR evaluation uses training annotations because official test labels lack radiologist IDs, its out-of-distribution group is an inferred co-annotation cluster, and no independent reproduction was performed.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of RACER’s theoretical implementation or synthetic and clinical benchmark results was found or performed.
Real-benchmark evidence does not establish clinical workflow benefit or patient outcomes; VinDr-CXR uses an inferred co-annotation-cluster OOD proxy and training-reader labels.
CheXpert comparisons are descriptive over 27 matched cells without significance tests; calibration metrics compare method-selected experts rather than fixed expert–query pairs.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently reproduced, a role-relative expert-competence estimator could improve routing when human expertise varies across cases and experts are unseen, a meaningful design issue in clinical decision systems. Score 5 reflects potential methodological value; preliminary benchmark comparisons and unverified deployment transfer do not establish clinical benefit.
limitations: All empirical results are author-reported from a work-in-progress preprint; the research desk did not reproduce them.
CheXpert’s 27-cell comparisons are descriptive, with no significance claim; reported calibration compares method-selected experts and is not a fixed-pair comparison.
VinDr-CXR official test labels are consensus-only and have no radiologist IDs; the paper evaluates training annotations with image/expert splits.
The inferred R8/R9/R10 co-annotation cluster is an out-of-distribution expert proxy, not a verified hospital/site identifier.
No clinical deployment, workflow-time, cost or patient-outcome effect is measured; code is stated to be released upon publication.
brief.summary: A September 18 work-in-progress preprint proposes RACER, which estimates an unseen expert’s query-level probability of being correct from a small context set using class-role relationships rather than absolute class identities. The authors prove a coherent class-relabelling invariance result, derive a Bayes-aligned deferral surrogate and provide a regret bound. In experiments, they report gains on synthetic expert benchmarks and budget-swept performance described as competitive or best on VinDr-CXR and CheXpert. On CheXpert, RACER-C and RACER-kernel report similar primary AURSBAC means (0.7243 and 0.7241 over 27 matched cells); the paper labels the comparisons descriptive and makes no significance claim. VinDr-CXR results use training annotations because official test labels lack radiologist identities; an out-of-distribution expert group is inferred from co-annotation patterns. technical.claimed_result: The authors report synthetic benchmark gains, including improved context-scaling under hidden subtype dependence and strongest aggregate routing on a separately sampled unseen-expert CIFAR-100 split. On real chest-radiography benchmarks, RACER variants are reported as competitive or best under budget-swept deferral. CheXpert primary AURSBAC means are 0.7243 for RACER-C and 0.7241 for RACER-kernel over 27 matched cells; no significance claim is made.
technical.compute_or_cost: No clinical cost, workflow-time, patient-outcome or deployment-economic measurements are reported. Code is stated to be released upon publication; the research desk did not execute the experiments.
technical.demonstrated_result: The work-in-progress preprint specifies the estimator, theoretical arguments, benchmark protocols and author-reported results. the research desk did not execute code or reproduce the theory or experiments; the paper says code will be released upon publication.
technical.mechanism: RACER estimates an unseen expert’s posterior-predictive correctness probability for a query under each candidate class role using context examples. Nonparametric and neural kernel-pooling estimators aggregate role-relative relations while excluding absolute class-identity channels, then combine competence estimates with the model posterior for deferral.
technical.regime: Work-in-progress preprint. Synthetic benchmarks include CIFAR-100 and PathMNIST with simulated experts. Real evaluations cover VinDr-CXR radiologist deferral and CheXpert human–AI multi-expert deferral. CheXpert uses three candidate human readers, three held-out AI choices and three seeds (27 matched cells). VinDr-CXR uses training annotations with disjoint image/expert splits; the inferred R8/R9/R10 co-annotation cluster is an OOD proxy, not a verified hospital label.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes synthetic and chest-radiography protocols and reports descriptive standard deviations, but code is not yet released in this version and results have not been independently reproduced.
technical.strongest_baseline: On CheXpert, the best non-RACER primary AURSBAC mean in the compact table is IFD-MLP at 0.7105, compared with 0.7243 for RACER-C and 0.7241 for RACER-kernel. The paper reports standard deviations over 27 cells and explicitly characterizes these comparisons as descriptive without significance tests.

brief.title: RACER reports role-based competence estimates for routing to unseen human experts
brief.why_it_matters: Routing systems need to estimate when a particular human expert is likely to outperform the model on a specific case, including experts unseen during training. If the role-relative interface generalizes, it could improve human–AI handoffs without learning shortcuts from label identities. The current clinical evidence is preliminary: CheXpert gains are descriptive without significance testing, VinDr-CXR uses a proxy for site shift, and no deployment outcome is measured.
